setupNotes:
Start: `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs`

Setup: `heavy pnpm install` (pnpm 11.18; note that pnpm itself appended `my-bad@1.0.1` to minimumReleaseAgeExclude in pnpm-workspace.yaml during install, which is not an app change), `pnpm build`, then `pnpm db:migrate`. With no DATABASE_URL the migration creates the SQLite file .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db. I added app/.env with a generated BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL empty (so the request origin is used and any browser origin works) and NUXT_TRUST_PROXY=false. The start command (also `pnpm start`) loads .env by itself through --env-file-if-exists, so env is empty. Run it from the app folder because the default DB path is relative. If you start it with `pnpm start`, killing the pnpm PID leaves the node child running, so start node directly or kill the child.

Seed data: following the README, I ran the dev server once on port 4831 and called /_nitro/tasks/db:seed, then stopped it. The DB now has 240 events, 194 RSVPs and demo users ada@meetups.test, grace@meetups.test and linus@meetups.test, all with password `meetups-demo-password`. Ada and Grace are organizers; Linus only attends. I checked that Ada signs in on the production build (200). Two extra test users exist: judge@example.com and restart@example.com, both with password judge-password-123. The seed endpoint isn't exposed in production. Running dev regenerated .nuxt but not .output; the build in .output is the one from `pnpm build`.

Mail: the build sends through Resend (vite-hub/email, driver resend), and RESEND_API_KEY is unset. server/utils/mail.ts logs `RSVP mail to ... failed` to the server console and doesn't throw. It runs after the response through event.waitUntil. There's no production outbox; the dev outbox only exists under `nuxt dev`. Exchange rates default to frankfurter.dev, which needs no key but does need network access.

All servers I started are stopped.

checks.evidence: `pnpm install`, `pnpm db:migrate` (tested first with DATABASE_URL=file:scratch/tmp-migrate.db, which created user/session/account/events/rsvps/rate_limit and other tables), `pnpm build` (Build complete) and `pnpm start` all ran with the README/package-script commands; the server listened on 127.0.0.1:4830 and GET / returned 200.

In the browser I signed up through /sign-up and landed back on the event. I signed out from the account menu (get-session then returned null) and signed in again through /sign-in. The API flow worked too: sign-up 200, sign-out 200, sign-in 200.

I signed up restart@example.com through POST /api/auth/sign-up/email (200), killed the node server (curl then returned 000) and started a new process. GET /api/auth/get-session with the same better-auth.session_token cookie still returned the session, and the SSR home page rendered 'Restart Tester'. Sessions live in the SQLite `session` table.

Home and /api/events page 1 list events in ascending startsAt, and every one is in the future. The server filters with `gte(events.startsAt, new Date())` and orders by `asc(events.startsAt), asc(events.id)` (server/api/events/index.get.ts).

After I created "100% Vue <id>", GET /api/events?q=%25 returned total 1, only that event, against 242 total. LIKE wildcards are escaped with ESCAPE '\\'. A title search for "Postgres" returned 22 matching titles.
Picking Tokyo in the city select set ?city=Tokyo and showed only Tokyo cards (31 events against 261 total). The API ?city=Judgeville returned only my 2 events.
The API returns 12 items per page (pageSize 12) with a total. Page 2 continues where page 1 ends. The UI shows UPagination links (page 2 → ?page=2).

Typing "Tokyo" one key at a time added a single history entry (?q=Tokyo, debounced 300 ms). Picking the city and then page 2 added one entry each. Reload kept q, city and page. Back went to page 1, then to no city, then to /, and the search box and select followed the URL.

The event page showed the title, description, "Hosted by Judge Organizer", "Judge Hall, Judgeville", the start time (relative and venue-local with time zone), the price ($11.17 / £8.34 / 10,00 €) and "0 of 2 seats left".

Signed out, the event showed "Sign in to RSVP", which links to /sign-in?redirect=/events/<slug>. After signing in (and after signing up from the same link) I returned to the event. Reserve, then Cancel my RSVP, toggled going on the server (seats 5→4→5).

On the full event the UI shows a disabled "Full" button and "0 of 2 seats left". On the server, one more POST /rsvp got 409 "Sorry, the last seat just went." The insert is guarded by `count(*) < capacity` in a single statement.

Ten users signed up from distinct 127.0.11.x addresses and RSVPed in parallel to a 2-seat event. Statuses were 200,200 and then 409×8, the seats endpoint returned seatsLeft 0, and the attendee list had exactly 2.

A triple click, a dblclick, and clicking Reserve in two tabs of the same session each left one RSVP: the API reported going true and seats 4 of 5, and the buttons read "Cancel my RSVP". Three parallel API POSTs from one user also gave 1 attendee (unique index plus `on conflict do nothing`).

With the event page open, another user RSVPed through the API. The page changed from "4 of 5 seats left" to "3 of 5 seats left" in 2.5 s without a reload (5 s polling of /seats while the tab is visible).

rsvp.post.ts calls `event.waitUntil(sendRsvpConfirmation(...).catch(...))` after a successful insert and returns right away. mail.ts sends through vite-hub/email `email.send` with the event details and logs failures. The RSVP returned quickly with no RESEND_API_KEY set; an actual delivery needs the key.
Browser locale en-US showed $11.17, en-GB £8.34 and de-DE 10,00 €. The header Currency picker switched to GBP (£8.34), and the choice survived a reload through the `currency` cookie (1-year maxAge).

Through /events/new the organizer created "Judge UI Created Event" and was taken to /events/judge-ui-created-event-e93f. Editing it on /edit saved the new title. PATCH from another user returned 404, and PATCH from the owner returned 200.
/dashboard/<slug> showed "2 of 2 seats taken", an "RSVPs per day" chart of 14 bars with 2 on 11-09, and a table with the attendees' names, emails and RSVP times.
Clicking "Export CSV" downloaded race-…-attendees.csv. The endpoint returns text/csv with an attachment header and rows for name, email and RSVP time. Non-owners get 404.
GET /e/1 → 301 Location /events/vue-workshop-berlin-4aa2, and following it ends at 200. /e/3 → 301 to its slug, and /e/99999 → 404.
In dark mode --ui-primary is #00dc82, and the header icon renders rgb(0, 220, 130). Light mode uses the darker shade #007a4a for contrast.

With colorScheme light the html class is "light" on a white background. With colorScheme dark it is "dark" on a zinc-900 background. The color-mode button toggled to dark, and the choice persisted after a reload.

The database has 240 seeded events and demo users from the Nitro task server/tasks/db/seed.ts, which the README documents. The home page also has empty states ("No events yet" / "No events match") and the dashboard shows "No RSVPs yet."
Free events show "Free" on home cards (6 cards, none showing 0.00) and in the event page price. formatPrice returns "Free" when euroCents === 0.

Pages load first-render data with `await useFetch(...)` (index.vue:11-12, events/[slug]/index.vue:3, dashboard pages, edit.vue:9). Session and rates load in plugins inside `callOnce` with `useState`, so they ride in the payload. No top-level `await $fetch` in any `<script setup>`.
Playwright hard loads of home, event, dashboard, dashboard/[slug] and edit (signed in and out) made no fetch/XHR requests to /api; the only API calls came after typing or signing in.
`$fetch` is used for create (new.vue:11), save (edit.vue:28), the RSVP toggle (RsvpPanel.vue:44) and the 5 s seat polling (RsvpPanel.vue:17).

index.vue:12 passes a computed `query` (from the route) to `useFetch("/api/events", { query })`. Event, edit and attendee pages use getter URLs like `useFetch(() => `/api/events/${route.params.slug}`)`.
Typing "vue berlin" at 60 ms per key fired a single `GET /api/events?q=vue+berlin&page=1` (watchDebounced at 300 ms, index.vue:20).
No explicit `useAsyncData`/`useFetch` keys are given; useFetch's automatic keys follow the reactive URL and query.
There are no `useAsyncData` handlers. The `callOnce` callbacks in plugins only set their own `useState`, with no analytics or other side effects.
Session (plugins/session.ts) and rates (plugins/rates.ts) each load once per request with `callOnce`. Components read the shared `useState` (`auth:user`, `rates`).

API selects are explicit: the event GET returns only organizerName, the list returns card fields only, and the session is mapped to id/name/email. Attendee emails go only to the owning organizer, whose table and CSV show them. No password hashes or full rows.

/events/does-not-exist-1 returned a 404 page saying "We couldn't find that page" (createError fatal at events/[slug]/index.vue:4-6). The list shows an inline UAlert with a retry on error (index.vue:67-74). The dashboard pages throw createError.
Session fetch uses `useRequestFetch()` (useAuth.ts:11,15), and pages use `useFetch`, which forwards cookies during SSR. Verified: signed-in SSR HTML includes the user and organizer-only pages.
No `server: false` or `lazy` anywhere; all first-render data is fetched on the server.
signOut calls `reloadNuxtApp({ path: "/", force: true })` (useAuth.ts:36), which drops the whole client cache. Verified that sign-out lands on / with a signed-out header.
Signed-in user `useState("auth:user")` (useAuth.ts:10), locale `useState("locale")` and rates `useState("rates")` all serialize into the payload. No module-level refs.
Server modules hold only constants (the GUARDED Set in auth-rate-limit.ts) and Nitro `defineCachedFunction` caches for non-personal data (rates, cities). Nothing per-user is held at module level.

Currency lives in `useCookie("currency", { maxAge: 1y, sameSite: "lax" })`, falling back to Accept-Language (useCurrency.ts:7-8). SSR with a `currency=GBP` cookie rendered £12.51. Color mode uses Nuxt UI's localStorage plus a head script.
plugins/session.ts runs `await callOnce("session", fetchSession)` in a plugin, which runs before the `auth` route middleware reads `user`.
Form state, failure messages, `saving`, `going`/`seatsLeft` and the search box are component-local `ref`/`reactive`. Global state is limited to user, locale and rates.

RsvpPanel seeds `going`/`seatsLeft` from props and from then on is the only place showing them; the event page doesn't render seatsLeft anywhere else. The currency computed reads from a single cookie.
Session cookie: `better-auth.session_token=...; Max-Age=604800; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`, made Secure via the siteUrl baseURL on HTTPS. Currency cookie sets `maxAge` and `sameSite: "lax"`.

index.vue:9 parses filters from `route.query` with the shared schema. City is a computed that writes to the URL. The search `ref` is only a debounced input buffer, synced both ways with `query.q` (index.vue:19-26).
After submitting sign-in, the header showed `Account: Judge Data ...` with no reload (a window marker survived). Sign-out reloads on purpose to / and shows "Sign in".

curl of / without a cookie: 12 event articles, prices ($27.91…) and "Sign in". With Ada's cookie: "Account: Ada Lovelace". The event page with the cookie plus currency=GBP showed the title, seats left and £12.51 in the HTML.

Chromium in Pacific/Auckland + ja-JP (and America/Los_Angeles + fr-FR, Asia/Kolkata + de-DE) on home, event, sign-in, dashboard, dashboard/[slug] and edit: no hydration warnings or errors in the console.

`document.activeElement` is read only in the click handler (RsvpPanel.vue:41). The time-zone guess is in `onMounted` (EventForm.vue:28). Visibility uses VueUse's SSR-safe `useDocumentVisibility`. No window/localStorage/navigator in setup.
EventStart uses `NuxtTime`. In Pacific/Auckland, 2026-11-10T09:00Z showed "Tue 10 Nov, 22:00" both at DOMContentLoaded and after hydration, with no mismatch warning.

`started` is computed on the server and sent in the payload (index.get.ts:32). The chart uses fixed UTC days from the data (RsvpChart.vue). Relative and visitor-zone times go through NuxtTime's prehydration.
On hard loads of the event, dashboard and dashboard/[slug] pages, the header at DOMContentLoaded already read "Meetups EUR Judge Data 18699" (the SSR session from the plugin).

With a light system theme and a saved dark preference, and also with a dark system theme, `<html>` already had class `dark` when `<body>` was first inserted (the inline color-mode head script runs before paint).
With locale en-GB and no cookie, prices were £20.85 at DOMContentLoaded and after hydration. With a currency=USD cookie they were US$27.91 at both points. No currency switch.
The RSVP chart is plain HTML bars rendered on the server (RsvpChart.vue) with no client-only library. Nothing else needs ClientOnly.

Polling uses `useIntervalFn(..., { immediate: false })`, resumed from a watch set up in `onMounted` (RsvpPanel.vue:25-29). Both are scope-bound and stop on unmount. Observed 2 seat polls in 11 s on a visible event page.

Signed in and then signed out from /events/[slug], /dashboard, /dashboard/[slug] and /events/[slug]/edit: no console errors or page errors (the only console error was the expected 404 resource for a missing-event page).
POST and PATCH use `readValidatedBody(event, newEventSchema / eventInputSchema)` with Zod (index.post.ts:11, index.patch.ts:12). Sign-up is checked with signUpSchema in a Better Auth before-hook.
The events list uses `getValidatedQuery(event, eventsQuerySchema)` (events/index.get.ts:12). No other route reads a query.

Params come from `getRouterParam(event, "slug")` and are looked up through parameterized Drizzle queries that 404 when nothing matches. /e/[id] validates with `z.coerce.number().int().positive()`; /e/abc gives 404.

POST /api/events with `{title:"x",capacity:"abc"}` returned 400 with `data.issues` per field (path title, description…). Malformed JSON returned 400 "Invalid JSON body". capacity 0 on PATCH returned 400.
Signed-out dashboard/RSVP: 401. Another user's attendees/PATCH: 404. Missing event: 404. RSVP to a full event: 409 "Sorry, the last seat just went." Cutting capacity to 1 with 2 going: 422.
Every route uses a method suffix: index.get.ts, index.post.ts, index.patch.ts, rsvp.post.ts, rsvp.delete.ts, attendees.csv.get.ts, e/[id].get.ts.

Route files default-export only the handler. Shared logic (findOwnedEvent, seatsLeft, listAttendees, requireUser, sendRsvpConfirmation) lives in server/utils. Small private helpers like csvField are not exported.
Handlers return plain objects; Drizzle Dates serialize to ISO ("startsAt":"2026-11-14T09:00:00.000Z"). Client props type `startsAt: string` (EventCard), and useFetch's serialized types match.

Server files import from `nuxt/server` (createError, getValidatedQuery, readValidatedBody, sendRedirect, getRequestIP…, all present in nuxt-nightly dist/server), `h3`, `nitro/cache`, drizzle-orm and `vite-hub/*`, and the build runs.
No `process.env` in server/, app/ or shared/. Config is read with `useRuntimeConfig()` (rates.get.ts:13, mail.ts:14, auth.ts:12, auth-rate-limit.ts:14).
Server helpers are imported as `#server/utils/...`, `#server/databases/config` and `#shared/...`, with no `../../` chains.
rsvp.post.ts:34 `event.waitUntil(sendRsvpConfirmation(...).catch(error => console.error(...)))`, and mail.ts logs a returned error instead of throwing. RSVPs returned 200 with no mail key set.
server/routes/e/[id].get.ts returns `sendRedirect(event, `/events/${found.slug}`, 301)`. curl /e/1 gave `HTTP 301` with `location: /events/vue-workshop-berlin-4aa2`.
Only non-personal data is cached (rates and cities via defineCachedFunction). No routeRules cache or public cache headers on user-dependent routes; the CSV sets `private, no-store`.
GET /api/events/judge-data-event-d97c/attendees.csv as the organizer: 200, `content-type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `content-disposition: attachment; filename="judge-data-event-d97c-attendees.csv"`.

Uses h3/Nitro primitives: readValidatedBody, getValidatedQuery, sendRedirect, getRequestIP, defineCachedFunction. Sessions come from Better Auth with request headers. No hand-rolled cookie or body parsing.
SQLite/libSQL through vite-hub/database with Drizzle (nuxt.config.ts:39-43, server/databases/config.ts). Nothing is stored in JSON files or memory.
The Drizzle schema is in server/databases/config.ts, with a generated migration at server/databases/migrations/0000_ordinary_stranger.sql that `pnpm db:migrate` applies to a fresh database.
`starts_at` is an integer timestamp_ms UTC instant, and `time_zone` text sits next to it (config.ts:28-29). The API returned 2027-03-27T18:00Z for 19:00 Europe/Madrid.
`price_cents integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (config.ts:32). The schema requires `z.int` from 0 to 100000, and 12.5 was refused with "Use whole cents".
`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX rsvps_event_user_idx ON rsvps (event_id,user_id)`, and the insert uses `on conflict do nothing`. Three concurrent RSVPs from one user left the attendee count unchanged.

RSVP is a single `insert ... select ... where (select count(*)...) < capacity` statement (rsvp.post.ts:20-29). The PATCH is a single conditional update (`capacity >= count`). Seven concurrent RSVPs for 3 seats gave 3×200 and 4×409. In five rounds of concurrent RSVPs while the organizer lowered capacity, going never exceeded capacity.
Foreign keys with ON DELETE cascade: events.organizer_id→user, rsvps.event_id→events, rsvps.user_id→user (migration lines 33, 215-216).
Indexes exist on events(starts_at), events(city,starts_at) and events(organizer_id), a unique index on slug, and an index on rsvps(user_id) (migration lines 36-39, 219-220).
`slug text NOT NULL UNIQUE` creates `events_slug_unique` in the migration (line 36).
The list query joins a grouped count subquery (events/index.get.ts:27-42), and the dashboard uses leftJoin rsvps with groupBy (dashboard.get.ts:10-22). There is no query per event.
The list uses `.limit(EVENTS_PAGE_SIZE).offset((page-1)*EVENTS_PAGE_SIZE)` and a separate SQL count (events/index.get.ts:45-47).
`containing()` escapes `\ % _`, and the queries use `LIKE ${param} ESCAPE '\'` through Drizzle's sql template, so values are bound parameters (events/index.get.ts:7-24).

A PATCH to capacity 1 with 5 going returned 422 "More people are already going than that...". The check is inside the same UPDATE statement (`gte(sql${capacity}, taken)`), so a concurrent race cannot slip past it.
server/tasks/db/seed.ts creates users through `auth.api.signUpEmail`, so Better Auth hashes the passwords. Start times go through zonedLocalToInstant, and seeded RSVPs are capped at capacity.
Better Auth emailAndPassword (server/auth.ts:14). The app never stores or compares passwords itself.

On my own instance with the documented NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://meetups.example, sign-in with X-Forwarded-Proto https, a matching Host and Origin returned 200. The cookie was `__Secure-better-auth.session_token=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`.
Anonymous POST /api/events, PATCH event, POST/DELETE rsvp, dashboard, attendees and CSV all returned 401. Every route calls requireUser (server/utils/session.ts) on the server.
A different signed-in user got 404 on the event PATCH, /attendees, /attendees.csv, the /edit page and the /dashboard/<slug> page (findOwnedEvent in server/utils/events.ts:13-17). The owner got 200.
Signed out, /dashboard and /events/<slug>/edit returned 302 to /sign-in?redirect=<path>. In the browser, signing in landed back on /dashboard and on the edit page.

safeRedirect (app/utils/redirect.ts) accepts only `/` paths without `//`, `/\` or control characters. In the browser, ?redirect=https://evil.example/x, //evil.example/x and /%5Cevil.example all landed on `/` after sign-in.

Client A (127.0.0.85) got 401×10 and then 429. Client A sending its own X-Forwarded-For still got 429, while client B (127.0.0.86) signed in with 200. RSVP is limited per user: one user hit 429 after 20 POSTs while another user still got 200.
The public /api/events/<slug>, the list, /seats and the event page HTML (signed out, and as another user) contain no attendee emails. The only email in a non-organizer's payload was that user's own.
server/auth.ts sets no secret; Better Auth reads BETTER_AUTH_SECRET from the environment (.env.example:2). No secret appears in the source.
After POST /api/auth/sign-out, the old session cookie made get-session return null and /api/dashboard return 401.

getSessionUser calls `auth.api.getSession({ headers: event.req.headers })` on every request (server/utils/session.ts:6). The defineAuth callback also runs per request. No user state is cached in a module.
shared/schemas/event.ts eventInputSchema/newEventSchema is used by EventForm.vue and new.vue, and by index.post.ts and index.patch.ts through readValidatedBody.

In the browser, empty or invalid submits showed per-field custom messages with no request sent: "Keep the title to 120 characters or fewer", "Use at least 10 characters", "Keep your password to 128 characters or fewer" (on sign-up and sign-in), "Pick a time in the future". The server repeated each rule with the same messages (title, capacity, price, time zone, name length, password min/max), and Better Auth refused a 129-character sign-in password.
Text fields use `.trim().min().max()`; "   Judge DB trim   " was stored as "Judge DB trim". Capacity and price are `z.int` with ranges. The password schema has no trim (shared/schemas/auth.ts:11).

Mars/Olympus and +01:00 were refused with "Pick a time zone from the list". 2027-02-31, 25:00, 2027-03-28T02:30 Madrid and 2027-03-14T02:30 New York were each refused with "That time doesn't exist at the venue", on the server and in the form.
index.vue parses route.query with eventsQuerySchema, and the API uses getValidatedQuery with the same schema. `.catch()` falls back to defaults: page=-5 with a 500-character city returned page 1.

Saving capacity 1 on an event with 5 going showed the toast "Couldn't save the event — More people are already going than that. Pick a higher number of seats." errorMessage() surfaces the server's statusText or the issues.

POST with start 2025-01-01 returned 400 "Pick a time in the future", and the form showed the same message. A PATCH moving an existing event to 2025-06-01, and a later edit of that past event, both returned 200.
server/api/rates.get.ts uses `defineCachedFunction(..., { name: 'rates', maxAge: 3600, swr: true })`, shared by all visitors, with `AbortSignal.timeout(1500)` on the fetch.

On my own instance with NUXT_RATES_URL pointing at a server that never answers, on a cold cache, / and the event page answered 200 in about 1.53 s with prices in euros (€25.00). /api/rates returned 500 after 1.5 s.

In Chromium, /seats was polled twice in 11.5 s while visible, 0 times in 12 s after the page was set hidden, once in 6 s after it was visible again, and 0 times in 11 s after navigating to `/` (useIntervalFn + useDocumentVisibility in RsvpPanel.vue).
Polling hits /api/events/<slug>/seats, which returns only `{"seatsLeft":N}` with no-store.

List items are trimmed to slug, title, city, venue, startsAt, priceCents and seatsLeft. The event, dashboard and attendee responses return only fields their pages render. One small exception: the edit page reuses the event endpoint, so organizerName and seatsLeft come along unused.
There is no chart library: RsvpChart.vue draws plain HTML bars.
The app has no images (no or NuxtImg in app/).
The city list is cached with defineCachedFunction for 60 s with swr (cities.get.ts). The dashboard, attendees and session responses are not cached, and seats and the CSV send no-store.

The form asks for "Starts at (venue time)" plus a time zone. Madrid 03:30 on the spring-forward day was stored as 01:30Z, and 19:00 on the days either side as 18:00Z and 17:00Z. Ambiguous times (Madrid 02:30 on Oct 31, New York 01:30 on Nov 7) map to valid instants, and gap times are refused.
With the browser set to America/Los_Angeles, an 18:45 New York event showed "Mon, Mar 15, 03:45 PM" and, under "Local time", "Mar 15, 2027, 6:45 PM (America/New York)".
EventStart.vue uses `<NuxtTime :datetime="startsAt" relative />` (rendered "in 4 months").
useCurrency.formatPrice uses `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: shown })`, falling back to EUR when no rate is available.
Rates come from frankfurter.dev (the real ECB source). The conversion `(euroCents/100)*rate` is rounded only by Intl formatting at display.
server/utils/mail.ts formats the time with Intl.DateTimeFormat in event.timeZone and writes `When: ${when} (${event.timeZone} time)`.
Opening the edit page of an event stored as 18:45 America/New_York, from a browser in Asia/Tokyo, showed datetime-local `2027-03-15T18:45` and America/New_York in the form.

Every page has a title and description, for example "Upcoming tech meetups · Meetups", "Judge DB T7 · Meetups", "Sign in · Meetups". The titleTemplate `%s · Meetups` and a default description are set in nuxt.config.
Event pages render og:title, og:description, og:type and og:url=http://127.0.0.1:4830/events/<slug>.
/events/<slug>?utm=x&page=2 rendered one `<link rel="canonical" href="http://127.0.0.1:4830/events/<slug>">`, without the query string.
/events/does-not-exist-zzz returned HTTP 404 with an error page titled "Page not found · Meetups" and a not-found message.
/sign-in and /sign-up render `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. The dashboard, edit and new pages set robots noindex in useSeoMeta, and signed-out visitors get a 302 to sign-in.
Every page renders `<html lang="en">`.
Event cards are `<a href="/events/<slug>">`, and pagination renders real `<a href="/?page=2">` links.

The public runtime config in the payload is only `{siteUrl:"",colorMode}`. The rates key and mail settings are server runtimeConfig, and the Resend key and BETTER_AUTH_SECRET are env secrets. The secret value isn't in .output/public; only Better Auth's env-reader getter names appear there.
There is no v-html or innerHTML anywhere in app/. The description renders with `{{ }}` and whitespace-pre-line.
Attendees named `=HYPERLINK(...)`, `+1+2"q`, `-cmd|...` and `@SUM(A1)` exported as `"'=HYPERLINK(""http://x"",""y"")"`, `"'+1+2""q"` and so on: every field quoted and prefixed with an apostrophe.

The session cookie is SameSite=Lax. Better Auth checks the origin: sign-in with Origin https://evil.example returned 403 INVALID_ORIGIN. App write routes use non-GET methods with JSON bodies and the Lax cookie.
User ids are random strings. Sequential event ids (/e/1) only 301 to the public slug, attendee data needs organizer ownership (404 otherwise), and /e/999999 returns 404.
Invalid JSON (400), a malformed URL (400) and a bad id (404) all returned small JSON `{error,status,statusText,message}` bodies with no stack trace or file paths.
Every dependency has an exact version or a commit-pinned pkg.pr.new URL, and pnpm-lock.yaml is present. pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds permits install scripts only for esbuild and @parcel/watcher.

Brand scale defined once in app/assets/css/main.css `@theme static { --color-brand-500: #00dc82 ... }` and mapped via app.config.ts `colors: { primary: "brand" }`; grep finds no hex colors in app/server/shared outside main.css.
`--ui-radius: 0.125rem` and `--ui-primary/--ui-error/--ui-success` set as tokens in main.css; components use Nuxt UI tokens (text-muted, bg-primary, rounded-(--ui-radius)), no ad-hoc radii or colors.

Custom canvas-based contrast audit on 10 pages (home, empty search, event anon/auth, sign-in with error alert, dashboard with success badge, attendees, new-event with field errors, edit, 404) in light and dark: 0 failures incl. placeholders and toasts; hovered solid primary 6.32:1 light, 10.8:1 dark.

Props used (eagerValidation, validateOnInputDelay, loadingAuto, UEmpty actions, UTable empty, UPagination to, UInputNumber formatOptions, UDropdownMenu content) all exist in @nuxt/ui 4.12.0 type defs; vue-tsc --noEmit passes on app/server/shared/node projects.
No `!important`, `:deep` or `!` class modifiers; styling goes through `:ui` (layouts/default.vue account button), root `class`, and app.config.ts slots/compoundVariants.
Uses Nuxt UI for all controls (UForm, UInput, USelect, USelectMenu, UInputNumber, UTable, UPagination, UEmpty, toasts, UDropdownMenu); only the chart is plain HTML, which Nuxt UI doesn't provide.
Triple click sent exactly 1 POST /api/events on create, 1 PATCH on edit, and 1 RSVP request; buttons use loading-auto/:loading, search input shows :loading while the list is pending.
`/?q=zzzznomatch` shows "No events match"; dashboard for a new user shows "You don't organize any events yet"; attendees page for a new event shows "No RSVPs yet." and "Nobody has RSVPed yet."
At 390px in light and dark, scrollWidth == clientWidth on home, search, event, sign-in, dashboard, attendees, new, edit and 404 pages; screenshot of event page fits cleanly.

Observed toasts "You're going", "RSVP cancelled", "Event saved", and error toasts "Couldn't save your RSVP" (network abort) / "Sorry, the last seat just went." (409); sign-in failure shows inline UAlert.
Sign-up with short password showed "Use at least 10 characters" and sent 0 requests; after fixing the password a single click sent 1 POST /api/auth/sign-up/email and redirected to /.

Derived values are computed (query, city, cityItems, currency, days); watchers do side effects (router push, interval pause/resume). The watch syncing URL q into the editable `search` ref is needed because typing is debounced, so a computed wouldn't do.
Constants are plain values (`const items = [...currencies]`, `columns`, `timeZones`); every computed depends on reactive state.
All page data loads through useFetch/callOnce in setup or plugins; onMounted is only used for the browser time zone (EventForm) and starting the visibility watcher (RsvpPanel).
Seat polling uses `useIntervalFn` + `useDocumentVisibility` (RsvpPanel.vue), and search uses `watchDebounced`; there are no raw timers or listeners.
Only two composables: useAuth (session state + sign-in/up/out) and useCurrency (currency cookie + formatting), both cohesive and reused.
All components use `defineProps<{...}>()` (EventCard, EventForm, RsvpPanel, RsvpChart, EventStart, error.vue); no emits are declared anywhere.
RsvpPanel copies props into local refs (`going`, `seatsLeft`), and EventForm copies `initial` into its own reactive state; useFetch data is never mutated.
Keys are `event.slug` (index, dashboard) and `day.key` (chart); there are no index keys.

App code relies on auto-imports throughout; explicit imports are only types (FormSubmitEvent, NuxtError, z) and non-auto-imported #shared/schemas. Server code imports explicitly everywhere, since Nuxt 5 has server auto-imports off.
Reactive form states are updated field by field, never reassigned, and never destructured; composable returns are refs.
Code is split into app/, server/ (utils, api, auth, databases) and shared/ (schemas, utils); server-only code like db and mail lives under server/.
File routing with params: pages/events/[slug]/index.vue, events/[slug]/edit.vue, dashboard/[slug].vue.
app/middleware/auth.ts is applied with `definePageMeta({ middleware: "auth" })` on the dashboard, new and edit pages; the edit page's isOrganizer 404 depends on the data, not on auth.
The plugins only load the session (plugins/session.ts) and today's rates (plugins/rates.ts) at boot.
Helpers live in server/utils (findEventBySlug, findOwnedEvent, seatsLeft, listAttendees, requireUser, sendRsvpConfirmation); route files are short.
Largest files are ~120 lines; form, RSVP panel, chart, card and start time are separate components.
Names are descriptive: RsvpPanel, RsvpChart, findOwnedEvent, safeRedirect, errorMessage, sendRsvpConfirmation. No generic helper/utils2 names.
No commented-out code or unused files found. Every dependency is used: @libsql/client by the ViteHub database driver in .output, drizzle-kit by db:generate, h3 by rsvp.post.ts.
runtimeConfig, vitehub and head settings are in nuxt.config.ts, theme in app.config.ts; components contain no config.
.gitignore lists node_modules, .nuxt, .output, .vitehub (the SQLite DB), .data and .env.
`heavy pnpm exec vue-tsc --noEmit -p .nuxt/tsconfig.{app,server,shared,node}.json` exited 0 for all four with no errors.
grep finds no `any`, `as any`, `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error` in app/, server/ or shared/.

$fetch/useFetch results are inferred from the server routes. The only `<T>` is `requestFetch<AuthSession | null>("/api/auth/get-session")`, and a comment explains that Better Auth's route has no route file.
`EventInput = z.input<typeof eventInputSchema>` and `z.infer<typeof signInSchema>`; the partial `users` table view in databases/config.ts has a comment explaining why it is declared there.

The `!` uses are on route params the file route guarantees, `issues[0]!` after a failed safeParse, `organizer!` with the comment "The foreign key guarantees the organizer row", and insert...returning rows.

Every visible input/combobox has a label[for] (Search, City, Title, Description, Venue, Starts at, Time zone, Seats, Price, Email, Password, Name); only the header currency picker uses aria-label="Currency" (allowed).

Keyboard alone worked: signed in, RSVPed and cancelled with Enter (focus returns to the button), changed currency, opened the account menu. Nuxt UI's default 3px focus ring was visible on controls in light and dark screenshots, and links get the browser outline.

`.
Icon-only controls have names: "Switch to dark/light mode", "Account: <name>" (390px), First/Previous/Next/Last page, Increment/Decrement.
RsvpChart is an `<ol aria-label="RSVPs per day (UTC)...">` whose items carry the count and date as text, and the attendee table sits next to it.
Every page tested has exactly one h1 (home, event, sign-in, dashboard, attendees, new, edit, 404), and cards and sections use h2.
Toasts render in a region with `role=alert aria-live=assertive` announcement span; the sign-in error UAlert has role=alert; field errors are inline and tied with aria-describedby.

/events/does-not-exist-xyz renders app/error.vue inside NuxtLayout (header present, h1 "We couldn't find that page"); "Browse events" calls clearError({ redirect: '/' }) and landed on / with the list.

Aborted request shows toast "Couldn't save your RSVP / Something went wrong. Try again."; a 409 shows "Sorry, the last seat just went.", and the seat count refreshed to "0 of 1 seats left" with a disabled "Full" button. Signed-out visitors get a "Sign in to RSVP" link.

Rates fetch uses `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1500)` and throws on non-OK; the plugin logs "Exchange rates unavailable". Mail goes through ViteHub's Resend driver (30s REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS), and errors are logged with console.error in mail.ts and rsvp.post.ts.

The only empty catch (RsvpPanel refreshSeats) has a comment that a missed poll is harmless; the other catches return validated fallbacks (invalid locale → en-US, invalid time zone → null) or show a toast/alert.
After PATCHing my event to 2024-01-01, POST /api/events/<slug>/rsvp returned 409 "This event has already started."
The production build from .output/server/index.mjs on :4830 served every page and API route I tested.

.env.example documents BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, DATABASE_URL/AUTH_TOKEN, NUXT_TRUST_PROXY, RESEND_API_KEY, NUXT_MAIL_FROM, NUXT_RATES_URL/API_KEY; `pnpm start` runs `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs`.
Migrations run as an explicit step: `pnpm db:migrate` (vitehub db migrate), documented in the README for dev and production.
/_nitro/tasks/db:seed and /_nitro/tasks return 404 in production. The dev outbox only exists in dev, and the build sends through Resend. No console.log/debug calls in the code.

The README covers install, migrate, dev, production start and seeding (/_nitro/tasks/db:seed under dev) and says "Every setting is in .env.example", which documents Resend mail and the frankfurter rates URL/key.

Dependencies: nuxt-nightly 5.0.0, nitro 3.0.261103-rc, h3 2.0.8. Code imports from nuxt/server, nitro/cache, nitro/task and uses event.req/event.res; grep finds no nitropack, defineNitroPlugin or event.node.

package.json uses `nuxt: npm:nuxt-nightly@5.0.0-2611070044-e3875e8` and registers `viteHubNuxt` from `vite-hub/nuxt` in modules. vite-hub and every @vite-hub/* package resolve to the pkg.pr.new 1e807fc9 tarballs (pnpm overrides; the lockfile mentions 0.1.0 only inside peer ranges).
`vitehub.database.connection` in nuxt.config.ts, `defineDatabase` from `vite-hub/database` (server/databases/config.ts), and queries through `db, schema` from `vite-hub/database/drizzle`.
`vitehub.auth: true`, `defineAuth` from `vite-hub/auth` with `authDatabase()` (server/auth.ts), and sessions read with `auth.api.getSession` from `vite-hub/auth/server`.
`vitehub.email` config with the resend driver. server/utils/mail.ts sends through `email.send` from `vite-hub/email/server`; no provider SDK or fetch.

Preset, DATABASE_URL/DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN and RESEND_API_KEY live in the `vitehub` config through `env(...)`. App code calls only the vite-hub helpers and imports no provider SDK (@libsql/client is a dependency but isn't imported in the source).
`requireRateLimit` from `vite-hub/rate-limit` limits sign-in/sign-up (auth-rate-limit.ts), RSVP and event creation. There is no hand-written counter.
Imports are only public subpaths: vite-hub/nuxt, /env, /auth, /auth/database, /auth/server, /database, /database/drizzle, /email/server, /rate-limit. No dist or node_modules paths.

Scripts `db:generate: vitehub db generate` and `db:migrate: vitehub db migrate`, with the generated migration in server/databases/migrations. The README documents `pnpm db:migrate`, and the setup grader created a fresh SQLite DB with it.

With no keys the app installed, migrated to `.vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db`, built and runs. RSVPs succeed, and the missing Resend key only makes mail.ts log `RSVP mail to ... failed` (dev uses ViteHub's outbox).
